rows.title: Quick search 'LIFE-1' lists LIFE-10…LIFE-17 and never LIFE-1 once a project has 8 or more longer keys ahead of it
rows.summary: Now: an issue whose key matches the query (ignoring case and spacing, so 'LIFE-1' and 'life 1' both count) is the first issue result, open or done. LIFE-1 therefore always shows ahead of LIFE-10…LIFE-16. Otherwise the order is unchanged: projects first, then issues matched by key, then issues matched by title, with open issues before done ones. The change is one sort key in src/utils/workspaceSearch.js. TopBar, WorkspaceLayout and WorkspaceRoute use this function and do not reorder its results.

rows.title: ATS plain text ignores the website/LinkedIn/GitHub 'Link URL' override, so a handle in the field loses the profile address
rows.summary: Now: when a website, LinkedIn or GitHub has a Link URL override, the ATS plain-text contact line (Export → ATS Text, and the ATS tab's Copy and Download) prints that override. It is the same address the PDF, Word and Markdown exports link to (contactHref). Without an override the line prints the value as typed, as R4-DOUT-13 set up. A Display label still never replaces the value. The override is printed only when contactHref gives a link. An override the PDF would not follow (javascript:, or one with spaces) returns no link, so the typed value prints instead. A hidden field and an empty field still print nothing, because contactItems filters them out first. Old stored data is safe: a missing, null or blank override falls back to the typed value.

rows.title: ATS Check says a phone field with more than 15 digits (two numbers or a long extension) is 'short' and tells the user to add an area code
rows.summary: Now: a phone field with more than 15 digits (the E.164 limit) gets the warning 'Phone field holds more than one number'. It is told to list a single reachable number, and it keeps the same 2 of 4 points. It is no longer called short or told to add an area or country code. 10–15 digits still pass, and 7–9 digits still get the short-number warning. A hidden phone still gets the 'hidden' failure, because shown() returns '' for it. Nothing in src/ reads the old warning text. The change is in src/utils/atsChecker.js.
